methodological_rigor.justification: Cell-based mechanistic study examining EXO1 role in nascent DNA degradation using multiple approaches: cell viability assays, DNA fiber analysis, replication fork assays, genetic manipulation (shRNA/CRISPR), and biochemical characterization. Appropriate controls comparing BRCA-proficient vs. proficient backgrounds. Statistical testing with P-values reported. Multiple independent replicates (n≥3 biological replicates). Limitations: limited in vivo tumor model validation, no clinical sample validation.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: Preclinical translational research identifying EXO1 overexpression as mechanism of genomic instability in BRCA-proficient cancers. Shows EXO1-mediated nascent DNA degradation creates genomic instability phenotype similar to BRCA inactivation. Identifies genomic instability source occurring in 'significant proportion' of tumors (more frequent than BRCA mutations). Directly relevant to understanding tumor evolution and therapy resistance mechanisms, with implications for personalized medicine approaches.

reporting_quality.justification: Comprehensive methods for DNA fiber analysis, replication fork visualization, cell culture, genetic engineering approaches, and biochemical assays. Standard protocols well-described with appropriate controls. Supplementary figures referenced. Some details on molecular modeling (AlphaFold predictions) could be more explicit. No explicit code or raw data deposition statement but methods sufficient for general reproduction.

novelty_literature.justification: Identifies EXO1 overexpression as driver of genomic instability in BRCA-proficient tumors, representing novel mechanism of replication stress-induced instability. Shows EXO1-MRE11 cooperation in nascent DNA degradation occurring independently of BRCA pathway, which is conceptually important. Mechanistic insight linking replication fork dynamics to genomic instability advances understanding of tumor evolution drivers.

writing_presentation.justification: Well-organized manuscript with clear progression from biological observation (EXO1 overexpression in tumors) through mechanistic characterization (EXO1-mediated DNA degradation) to functional consequences (genomic instability, genotoxic sensitivity). Figures effectively communicate DNA fiber analysis results and replication fork assays. Methods comprehensive. Discussion appropriately contextualizes findings within DNA repair and genomic instability literature.

key_strengths: Identifies EXO1 overexpression as driver of genomic instability in BRCA-proficient cancers, occurring more frequently than BRCA mutations in tumors
Mechanistic clarity: EXO1-mediated nascent DNA degradation at ssDNA gaps and reversed replication forks creates genomic instability phenotype
Demonstrates EXO1-MRE11 cooperation operates independently of BRCA pathway, explaining genomic instability in BRCA-proficient backgrounds
Functional consequence: EXO1 overexpression increases sensitivity to genotoxic agents, suggesting therapeutic vulnerability
key_concerns: Limited in vivo validation; xenograft models or clinical patient samples not analyzed to confirm EXO1-driven instability in actual tumors
Frequency and distribution of EXO1 overexpression across cancer types not comprehensively surveyed; 'significant proportion' not quantified across cohorts
Therapeutic implications speculative; no direct testing of EXO1 inhibition or targeting strategies in tumor models
Clinical sample validation absent; biomarker development for identifying EXO1-high tumors not addressed
chief_reviewer.rationale: Tier 2 paper: excellent mechanistic work identifying actionable driver of genomic instability with clear clinical implications. Requires in vivo validation and clinical sample analysis before therapeutic development. Strong foundation for future translational studies; appropriate for high-impact cancer journal.
